# Definition
**(i)** A space $(X, \mathscr{T})$ is said to have a ***countable basis*** at $x$ if there is a collection $\mathcal{B}_x \subset \mathcal{U}_x = \{ U \in \mathscr{T} \mid x \in U \}$ such that 

1. $\mathcal{B}_x$ is countable

2. $\forall U \in \mathcal{U}_x, \exists B \in \mathcal{B}_x$ such that $x \in B \subset U$.

**(ii)** A space $X$ is said to be ***first-countable*** if $X$ has a countable basis at every $x \in X$.

**(iii)** A space $X$ is said to be ***second-countable*** if $X$ has a countable basis for $\mathscr{T}$.

# Reference
- James R. Munkres. (2000). Topology (2nd ed.). Pearson.
